claim: County Business Patterns covers only employer establishments with paid employees and excludes non-employer businesses like solo dog walkers
notes: CBP basic data items are extracted from the Business Register for establishments with paid employees; excludes solo/informal workers.

claim: FRED series CUSR0000SS61031 is a national price index for pet food and treats and cannot report local daycare or grooming prices
calculation: index level relative to base Dec 1997=100
notes: National index of pet food & treats; not local dollars and does not cover grooming or daycare.

claim: Census American Community Survey does not measure pet ownership counts or household pet care expenditure
notes: ACS collects demographic, housing, and economic data; does not collect pet counts or pet spending.

claim: Warwick and Monroe median household incomes have overlapping 90 percent margins of error and cannot be statistically ranked
geography: Warwick town vs Monroe town (Orange County NY)
notes: Warwick CI ($109,075-$126,285) overlaps Monroe CI ($102,356-$129,682); difference is within survey error.

claim: CBP About documentation distinguishes the detailed operational scope between NAICS 812910 pet care and 541940 veterinary services
notes: Not confirmed by the source: CBP About page only lists broad exemptions (e.g. NAICS 111, 482) and does not define 6-digit NAICS scopes.

claim: ACS shows Warwick town has roughly 4491 pet-owning households
notes: Refuted: Census ACS collects demographic and housing data but does NOT measure pet counts or pet ownership; 4,491 is an AI hallucination.

claim: Orange County has 40 veterinary establishments so mobile groomers face 40 direct competitors
notes: Refuted: 40 establishments are clinical veterinary services (NAICS 541940), not mobile groomers or daycare (NAICS 812910 has 24 establishments); they are not direct competitors.

claim: U.S. pet spending is rising so Monroe town residents are spending more on pet care
notes: Unsupported: Ecological fallacy; national pet commodity inflation cannot establish that Monroe town residents are spending more on pet care.

claim: 19.38% of Warwick town households are renters so they are more likely to buy grooming
notes: Proxy: 19.38% renter rate is accurately measured from ACS, but the behavioral assertion that renters buy more grooming is an unverified proxy without empirical evidence.

claim: The pet food and treats CPI moved from 191.485 to 194.485 (1.57%) over twelve months
notes: Proxy: Mathematical calculation is verified against FRED, but it measures national pet food commodity inflation rather than local pet daycare/grooming service prices.

claim: Monroe town median household income is $116019 +- $13663 and Warwick town is $117680 +- $8605
